title: mitmweb flow update path: HTTP PUT -> view.update -> websocket broadcast
answers: How do UI flow edits get applied in mitmweb?
How are websocket updates pushed to the mitmweb frontend?
Where is the flows list endpoint handled?
body:
- Routes: module-level `handlers` in mitmproxy/tools/web/app.py (`/flows` -> `Flows`, `/flows/<id>` -> `FlowHandler`, `/updates` -> `ClientConnection`).
- List: `Flows.get` returns `[flow_to_json(f) for f in self.view]`; `flow_to_json` defines the JSON shape sent to the UI.
- Edit: `FlowHandler.put` does `flow.backup()`, iterates JSON keys; `request`/`response` fields are whitelisted (method/scheme/host/path/http_version as str, port int, headers/trailers cleared+re-added, content via `.text`), `marked`/`comment` set directly, unknown key -> `APIError(400)`. On `APIError` it calls `flow.revert()` and re-raises (other exceptions like ValueError from int() do NOT revert). On success `self.view.update([flow])`.
- Push: view emits `sig_view_update` -> `WebMaster._sig_view_update` (master.py) -> `ClientConnection.broadcast_flow("flows/update", flow)`. Other messages: flows/add, flows/remove, flows/reset, events/add, options/update, state/update.
- `WebSocketEventBroadcaster.open` registers connection + per-connection asyncio.Queue and `send_task`; `send` is put_nowait so slow clients don't block. `_broadcast_flow` adds per-connection `matching_filters`.
- Client->server: `ClientConnection.on_message` only accepts `flows/updateFilter`; anything else closes with 1011.
- Base class `RequestHandler`: `flow` property (404 APIError), `json` property (400 unless application/json).
